messages.content:
You answer a question about machines at work (law, guidance, manufacturers' manuals, company and plant
documents) using ONLY the numbered passages given. Each passage is headed by its document, its place and its rank.

Rules:
- Use only the passages. Do not use anything you know from elsewhere.
- Answer only if a passage states the answer for the exact subject asked about (the same device, the same article
  and paragraph, the same kind of verification, the same deadline). A passage about a neighbouring subject does not
  answer the question: then the kind is "unknown" and the value is null. A question about something that happened
  (the date of the last check, whether something is overdue today) is "unknown" unless a passage records that event.
- A passage marked "corrected by the corrigendum" already shows the corrected wording: reason with it. The old
  wording, given in the mark, is no longer valid.
- If the question asks about a day, compare that day with every date in the passages, one by one. A repeal or an
  application "from" a date takes effect on that date, not earlier: an act repealed from a date is still fully in
  force on every earlier day; a rule applying from a date does not yet bind on earlier days.
- When passages of different rank disagree, the higher rank wins: law, then guidance, then manufacturer's manual,
  then company procedure, then plant record. Between two Italian texts, a legislative decree (D.Lgs.) wins over a
  ministerial decree (DM). Say which one wins.
- A row of a table belongs to the thing named in that same row. Read the row of the item asked about, not a
  neighbouring row. When the question itself states a condition ("if it were in regular use", "built in 2017"),
  reason with that condition.
- The kind follows the question: "from which date / by which date / when (a day)" is "date"; "how often / for how
  long / within what time" is "duration"; "can / may / is / does / must" is "boolean"; "which / what (several
  things)" is "set"; who, why, under which condition is "text" (one short sentence naming every element asked for).
- Point at the evidence: for every passage you rely on, copy word for word the sentence, or the table row, that
  states what you use. Copy exactly, without changing a character; do not join text from two places.
- Return JSON only, with the reasoning first:
  {"reasoning": "what the passages say and how it leads to the answer, in a few short sentences",
   "kind": "set|date|duration|boolean|text|unknown",
   "value": <list of short strings for set | "YYYY-MM-DD" for date | ISO 8601 duration like "P10Y", "P6M", "P45D", "PT1H" | true/false | a short text | null>,
   "text": "one or two sentences for a person, naming the document and the article, section or page",
   "evidence": [{"passage": <number>, "quote": "<copied exactly from that passage>"}]}

Today is 2026-11-14.
Question: A machine was built and its EC declaration of conformity signed on 10 January 2027, but it is made available on the Union market for the first time on 25 January 2027. Which act governs its placing on the market: Directive 2006/42/EC or Regulation (EU) 2023/1230?

Passages:
[0] REG, Art. 52(1) — rank: law — corrected by the corrigendum (Corrigendum, point 6: '14 January 2027' now reads '20 January 2027'; Corrigendum, point 7: '13 July 2023' now reads '19 July 2023')
Article 52 Transitional provisions. 1. Member States shall not impede the making available on the market of products which were placed on the market in conformity with Directive 2006/42/EC before 20 January 2027. However, Chapter VI of this Regulation shall apply, from 19 July 2023, mutatis mutandis to such products instead of Article 11 of that Directive, including products for which a procedure has already been initiated under Article 11 of Directive 2006/42/EC.

[1] REG, Recital 1 — rank: law
(1) Directive 2006/42/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 3 ) was adopted in the context of establishing the internal market, in order to harmonise health and safety requirements for machinery in all Member States and to remove obstacles to trade in machinery between Member States.

[2] REG, Annex V, Part B, point 9 — rank: law
9. Additional information: Signed for and on behalf of: … (place and date of issue): (name, function) (signature): ( 1 ) It is optional for the manufacturer to assign a number to the declaration of conformity. ( 2 ) It is optional to assign a number to the declaration of conformity. ( 3 ) Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 June 2023 on machinery and repealing Directive 2006/42/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council and Council Directive 73/361/EEC ( OJ L 165, 29.6.2023, p. 1 ).

[3] REG, Recital 7 — rank: law
(7) Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 5 ) sets out rules on market surveillance and control of products entering the Union market. As Directive 2006/42/EC is listed in Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020, that Regulation already applies to products within the scope of this Regulation. However, Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 applies to products within the scope of this Regulation insofar as there are no specific provisions with the same objective, which regulate in a more specific manner particular aspects of market surveillance and enforcement.

[4] REG, Recital 8 — rank: law
(8) Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 lays down the tasks of economic operators regarding products subject to certain Union harmonisation legislation. It also provides that such products are to be placed on the market only if there is an economic operator established in the Union who is responsible for those tasks. That Union harmonisation legislation includes Directive 2006/42/EC. As a result, products within the scope of this Regulation are to be placed on the market only if there is an economic operator established in the Union who is responsible for the tasks set out in Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 in respect of those products.

[5] eu-reg-2024-1689, Art. 113 — rank: law
Article 113 Entry into force and application This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union . It shall apply from 2 August 2026. However: (a) Chapters I and II shall apply from 2 February 2025; (b) Chapter III Section 4, Chapter V, Chapter VII and Chapter XII and Article 78 shall apply from 2 August 2025, with the exception of Article 101; (c) Article 6(1) and the corresponding obligations in this Regulation shall apply from 2 August 2027.

[6] eu-dir-2014-35, Recital 24 — rank: law
(24) In order to ensure legal certainty, it is necessary to clarify that rules on Union market surveillance and control of products entering the Union market provided for in Regulation (EC) No 765/2008 apply to electrical equipment. This Directive should not prevent Member States from choosing the competent authorities to carry out those tasks.

[7] eu-reg-2023-988, Art. 52 — rank: law
Article 52 Entry into force and application This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union . It shall apply from 13 December 2024.

[8] eu-dir-2009-104, Recital 10 — rank: law
(10) Pursuant to Directive 98/34/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 22 June 1998 laying down a procedure for the provision of information in the field of technical standards and regulations and of rules on Information Society services ( 6 ) , Member States are required to notify the Commission of any draft technical regulations relating to machines, equipment and installations.

[9] REG, Art. 21(3) — rank: law
Article 21 EU declaration of conformity of machinery and related products. 3. Where machinery or a related product is subject to more than one Union legal act that requires an EU declaration of conformity, a single EU declaration of conformity shall be drawn up in respect of all such acts. That declaration shall contain the identification of the Union legal acts concerned, including their publication references.

[10] REG, Art. 54 — rank: law — corrected by the corrigendum (Corrigendum, point 10: '14 January 2027' now reads '20 January 2027'; Corrigendum, point 11: '14 January 2024' now reads '20 January 2024'; Corrigendum, point 12: '14 October 2023' now reads '20 October 2026'; Corrigendum, point 13: '13 July 2023' now reads '19 July 2023'; Corrigendum, point 14: '14 July 2024' now reads '20 July 2024')
Article 54 Entry into force and application This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union . It shall apply from 20 January 2027. However, the following Articles shall apply from the following dates: (a) Articles 26 to 42 from 20 January 2024; (b) Article 50(1) from 20 October 2026; (c) Article 6(7) and Articles 48 and 52 from 19 July 2023; (d) Article 6(2) to (6), (8) and (11) and Articles 47 and 53(3) from 20 July 2024.

[11] eu-dir-2014-30, Recital 47 — rank: law
(47) In order to ensure legal certainty, it is necessary to clarify that rules on Union market surveillance and control of products entering the Union market provided for in Regulation (EC) No 765/2008 apply to apparatus covered by this Directive. This Directive should not prevent Member States from choosing the competent authorities to carry out those tasks.

response.text: {"reasoning": "Passage 10 (Art. 54, corrected by the corrigendum) says the Regulation applies from 20 January 2027. Passage 0 (Art. 52(1)) only protects products placed on the market in conformity with Directive 2006/42/EC before 20 January 2027. The machine was first made available on the Union market on 25 January 2027, which is after that date, so the transitional protection does not apply. The signing date of the EC declaration (10 January 2027) does not decide the question; the placing on the market does. Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 therefore governs.", "kind": "text", "value": "Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 governs, because the machine is first placed on the market on 25 January 2027, after the 20 January 2027 date and outside the Directive 2006/42/EC transitional protection.", "text": "Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, Article 54, applies from 20 January 2027, and the Article 52(1) transitional protection for Directive 2006/42/EC covers only products placed on the market before that date, so this machine falls under the Regulation.", "evidence": [{"passage": 10, "quote": "It shall apply from 20 January 2027."}, {"passage": 0, "quote": "Member States shall not impede the making available on the market of products which were placed on the market in conformity with Directive 2006/42/EC before 20 January 2027."}]}
